newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major questions size of Labour poll lead.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major questions size of Labour poll lead.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said he was unconcerned about the decision of the mass circulation Sun newspaper to back the opposition Labour party and also questioned the size of Labour's opinion poll lead.
"I am unconcerned about the Sun's editorial position," he told GMTV television. "All I ask of the Sun and other newspapers is that they report fairly and adequately what we say and do."
The Sun, Britain's best-selling newspaper, threw its weight behind Labour leader Tony Blair, saying people needed "a leader with vision, purpose and courage who can fire their imaginations."
The tabloid, owned by Australian-born Rupert Murdoch, backed Major in the 1992 election.
Asked about polls showing Labour with a 28-point lead in opinion polls, Major said:
"I really doubt that. I have lived through bad opinion polls through most of the last six years -- indeed before the last general election the polls were pretty awful."
Major said that four days before the 1992 election, polls were predicting a substantial Labour win. "It wasn't that way when people actually went into the polling booths to make up their mind."
